answer: To resist sybil attacks, an agent economy can require cost-bound identity staking: each agent locks a small deposit, like a pearl of real value, before beginning a commercial voyage. A reputation operator scores verifiable transaction history instead of mere account counts, much like a merchant telling genuine saffron from fakes by aroma and origin certificates. Forging thousands of identities becomes uneconomical because each fake must lock real capital, while honest agents recover their deposits intact once good behavior is proven.
